newsitem.title: UK: Sheffield Wednesday FC put float plans on hold.
newsitem.headline: Sheffield Wednesday FC put float plans on hold.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Sheffield Wednesday announced plans to raise 17 million stg via a placing and open offer on Wednesday but said that it would not be joining the stock market for two or three years.

Venture capital group Charterhouse Development Capital Funds is to be among new investors in the club. It is expected to subscribe to 8.5 million stg worth of shares to take a 20 percent stake in Wednesday.

"It is considered that the objective for the company should be a full listing on the London Stock Exchange but it is likely to be more beneficial to achieve this in two or three years' time," Wednesday chairman David Richards said.

"An immediate listing would not be possible as, amongst other things, the company would first need to make appointments of key full-time executives. Further, the performance of the company in 1996 has been weaker relatively than in 1994," he added in a letter to shareholders.
"It is hoped that the proceeds for the placing and open offer will allow the company to improve its performance and so provide a stronger prospect for flotation."

The initial euphoria surrounding floated soccer clubs has evaporated in recent weeks. Share prices have fallen, particularly among the mid-ranking premier league clubs and the smaller first division teams.
The flotation of first division Charlton Athletic CLO.L on the Alternative Investment Market last week illustrates the trend, the shares trading at a substantial discount to their issue price.

The 17 million stg which Sheffield Wednesday plan to raise will be used to strengthen the squad, improve the club's training ground and Hillsborough stadium and cut borrowings nad boost working capital.
Shareholders can apply for offer shares at 85p each and the deal values the club at a total 42.5 million stg. The club said there would be a matched bargain dealing facility for shares.
Wednesday, a medium-sized club by premier league standards, are enjoying a good season and are pushing for a place in next season's UEFA Cup.
